title: unittest.mock.patch()
summary: Temporarily replace an object with a mock, restoring it afterwards — as a decorator, a context manager, or manually.
description: Patch **where the name is looked up**, not where it is defined. If `myapp.service` does `from requests import get`, you patch `myapp.service.get` — patching `requests.get` will not affect the already-bound name.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: Dotted path to the name as the code under test resolves it.

parameters.name: autospec
parameters.description: Build the mock from the real signature, so wrong calls fail.

parameters.name: return_value / side_effect
parameters.description: What the mock returns, or an exception/callable to invoke.

returns: A MagicMock, injected or bound as the context variable.

raises.when: The target path does not exist — which is the usual sign of patching the wrong place.

examples.title: As a context manager
examples.code:
from unittest.mock import patch
import os

with patch.dict(os.environ, {'MODE': 'test'}):
    print(os.environ['MODE'])
print('MODE' in os.environ)

examples.title: Asserting how it was called
examples.code:
from unittest.mock import MagicMock
send = MagicMock(return_value=1)
send('GET', '/things')
send.assert_called_once_with('GET', '/things')
print('call recorded')

examples.title: Raising, to test the failure path

real_world_usage: Simulating a network failure, freezing time, avoiding a real email send in tests, and asserting an external call was made with the right arguments.

common_mistakes.mistake: Patching where the object is defined
common_mistakes.fix: Patch where it is *used*. This is the single commonest mock error.
A plain MagicMock accepts any call, so a signature change leaves the test passing against code that is now broken.

common_mistakes.mistake: Mocking the thing you are testing
common_mistakes.fix: Then the test asserts your mock works. Mock at the boundary only.

common_mistakes.mistake: Reaching for a mock when injection would do
common_mistakes.fix: Passing a fake collaborator in is simpler, faster and survives refactoring — see the api-client-sdk project.

performance_notes: Mocks are fast; over-mocking is slow to *maintain*. Tests that mock deeply break on every refactor.
security_notes: Use patch.dict for environment variables so real secrets are never read, and never let a test fall through to a live endpoint.
